AUS.hook: The only country that is also a continent, and more than 80% of its mammals, reptiles and frogs live nowhere else.
AUS.place: The continent-sized island between the Indian and Pacific oceans, below Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.
AUS.borders: A whole continent claimed by Britain, so its only land lines are internal state borders; the external boundary that needed drawing — through the Torres Strait, where Australian islands sit within sight of Papua New Guinea — took a careful 1978 treaty.

NZL.hook: One of the last large landmasses humans reached, settled only around 1300 — and it had no land mammals at all except bats.
NZL.place: Two main islands about 2,000km southeast of Australia, alone in the South Pacific.
NZL.borders: Two main islands with no neighbour within 1,500 km, annexed by Britain under the 1840 Treaty of Waitangi — the only boundary questions are maritime, plus free-association ties to the Cook Islands and Niue.
